message.content: {"answer":[{"text":"Personality measures should be used as an adjunct to biochemical indicators, not as a stand-alone way to infer historical brain injury. [7,8]","evidence_ids":[7,8]},{"text":"In the mTBI study, hair cortisol was not associated with long-term post-traumatic symptoms or functional recovery, and it did not support use as a marker of stress in mTBI. [7]","evidence_ids":[7]},{"text":"The retrospective TBI recommendations state that blood-based biomarkers and performance-based measures alone lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity to detect past TBI, so they should not be used in isolation for retrospective classification. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"The same recommendations emphasize that self/proxy-report and medical record abstraction are the methods with sufficient evidence for characterizing prior TBI history, while biomarkers are still nascent. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"The evidence suggests that wide-angle retinal-image models can transfer some learned features across retinal diseases, because a model trained on ultra-wide-field fundus images for macular holes was described as focusing on general and flexible features and was also discussed alongside prior wide-angle deep-learning work for diabetic retinopathy and retinal detachment. [5,9]","evidence_ids":[5,9]},{"text":"However, the evidence also shows that transfer is not guaranteed across diseases, since the macular-hole study only evaluated normal eyes versus macular holes and explicitly noted that it did not assess other fundus diseases. [5]","evidence_ids":[5]},{"text":"The diabetic retinopathy study likewise focused on treatment-naïve proliferative diabetic retinopathy versus non-DR images, so it supports disease-specific success rather than direct cross-disease transfer. [9]","evidence_ids":[9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"The electrode material can be chosen to improve rate capability by lowering electrode resistivity and/or thickness, which the RPC studies identify as key levers for higher counting rates. [6]","evidence_ids":[6]},{"text":"Using thin phenolic glass electrodes with a 0.2 mm gas gap gave a compact detector of about 8.2 mm total thickness, but the study notes that further optimization is needed to balance tracking, timing, and rate capability. [6]","evidence_ids":[6]},{"text":"The same study reports that reducing electrode thickness and resistivity is part of the strategy for rate capability, while timing can be improved by reducing gap thickness and optimizing the front-end electronics. [6]","evidence_ids":[6]},{"text":"A GaAs-based resistive electrode prototype achieved high rate capability and very low dark count rate, and the authors note that further electrode metallization optimization is needed to maximize charge collection without losing acceptance and time response. [5]","evidence_ids":[5]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Early stakeholder conflict resolution can prevent policy formulation and implementation from stalling when powerful actors have divergent positions, because unresolved conflicts were linked to halted or delayed implementation in the Ghana adolescent health cases.","evidence_ids":[5]},{"text":"Structured dialogue and early, inclusive stakeholder mapping can surface hidden conflicts, align interests, and reduce the risk that policies deviate from their original design during implementation.","evidence_ids":[5]},{"text":"Engaging stakeholders early also helps tailor content and implementation to local values and norms, which can improve acceptance of gender-sensitive policy and reduce backlash from communities or institutions.","evidence_ids":[3,5]},{"text":"The evidence suggests that when consensus and collaboration are achieved early, implementation is smoother, as seen in the Safety Net programme, whereas unresolved contestation led to resistance in other cases.","evidence_ids":[5]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Aligning workplace-focused language curricula with industry standards helps students master industry-specific English terminology, communication strategies, and business processes, which improves their workplace competitiveness and adaptability.","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"Such alignment can also shorten the transition from campus to workplace by exposing learners to practical work scenarios and the problems they may face in future jobs.","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"Practical English programs that match workplace needs can improve English communication, cross-cultural communication, information processing, and professional-field language use, which supports better job performance.","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"The evidence also suggests that curriculum alignment should include updated course content, stronger teacher industry knowledge, practical teaching, and assessment methods to better meet workplace expectations.","evidence_ids":[9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Patients with four or more gastrointestinal symptoms had markedly lower food-related quality of life, suggesting they need targeted dietary support.","evidence_ids":[3,9]},{"text":"Younger patients had worse food-related quality of life, so they may benefit from targeted psychosocial support.","evidence_ids":[3,9]},{"text":"In inflammatory bowel disease, patients with Crohn’s disease, stricturing disease, and prior IBD-related surgery had significantly lower food-related quality of life and should be targeted for support.","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"Higher disease activity and greater IBD-related disability were also associated with lower food-related quality of life, indicating these patients may need additional support.","evidence_ids":[9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Teacher development is best enabled by contextualized curriculum design, adaptive training, and collaboration among schools, communities, and parents.","evidence_ids":[4,6]},{"text":"Continuous professional development and training in digital literacy, technology use, and technology-based pedagogy are emphasized as key supports for MI teachers.","evidence_ids":[4,6]},{"text":"A participatory literacy ecosystem that includes literacy habituation, teacher-as-facilitator roles, and stakeholder synergy is recommended to strengthen teacher professionalism.","evidence_ids":[4,6]},{"text":"Providing educational technology and integrating digital literacy into learning can improve teacher readiness for technology-ready schools.","evidence_ids":[6,4]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Combining physical inspection with measured speed data helps diagnose gear faults because inspection can reveal gear type, wear, damage, backlash, or abnormal behavior, while speed measurements let you compare actual transmission ratios and detect discrepancies from expected gear-train performance. [6,9]","evidence_ids":[6,9]},{"text":"In the gear experiments, students inspect and disassemble gear systems, count teeth, and measure motor and output shaft speeds with a laser tachometer to predict train ratios and explain mismatches, which directly supports fault diagnosis. [9]","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"The laboratory also emphasizes distinguishing normal from worn components and recognizing warning signs of faulty bearings and gearbox behavior, showing why visual inspection complements quantitative speed checks. [6]","evidence_ids":[6]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"The evidence does not address whether early ventilator parameters can guide the choice of noninvasive oxygen support to reduce mortality in the specific clinical scenario asked.","evidence_ids":[3,4]},{"text":"One study found that values at 24 hours of PEEP, plateau pressure, FiO2, tidal volume, and extrapulmonary organ failures predicted ICU mortality in ventilated acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, but it did not test noninvasive oxygen support selection.","evidence_ids":[3]},{"text":"In COPD patients with severe COVID-19, high-flow nasal cannula was associated with lower 90-day mortality than invasive mechanical ventilation, while non-invasive mechanical ventilation was not significantly associated with mortality reduction.","evidence_ids":[4]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Selective source summaries can be built by extracting only the source parts relevant to each target word, so the decoder retrieves a small context instead of encoding the whole sentence into one fixed vector, which supports low-latency translation and better handling of long sentences.","evidence_ids":[2,8]},{"text":"The attention mechanism computes a separate context vector for each target word by softly selecting source annotations, so only the most relevant source information is used at each step.","evidence_ids":[2,8]},{"text":"A simultaneous greedy decoding strategy can start translating before the full source sentence is received, and it controls the delay-quality trade-off with adjustable waiting criteria.","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"Quality control can be added by waiting only when the next source chunk changes the best target word or lowers its confidence, which helps balance delay against translation quality.","evidence_ids":[8]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"A positive or neutral mealtime atmosphere was associated with greater use of structure-based feeding practices such as sitting and eating with the child, choosing where the child ate, and involving the child in deciding what foods to eat.","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"The review also reports that positive mealtime atmosphere was linked to more structure-based practices like modelling and meal/snack routines, which were in turn positively associated with preschoolers’ fruit and vegetable consumption.","evidence_ids":[6,9]},{"text":"Overall, a positive mealtime atmosphere may support preschoolers’ produce consumption indirectly by encouraging adaptive feeding practices that are associated with higher fruit and vegetable intake.","evidence_ids":[6,9]}]}
